8ball.title: Let the Ferry Terminal Decide Your Whole Day
8ball.description: Go to the Casco Bay Lines terminal, take the very next boat that leaves to whichever island it is bound for, and stay until the return run.
8ball.bonus: Do not look up a single thing about the island before you land on it.

8ball.title: Eat Only What the Counter Tells You To, All Day
8ball.description: Three meals across Portland and no menus — at each place, ask whoever is behind the counter what you should order, and eat exactly that.
8ball.bonus: Include one thing you would normally refuse outright.

social.title: Pick From 400 Beers at Novare Res Bier Café
social.description: Find the hidden alley off Exchange Street and take a picnic table on the terrace with a beer list four hundred long.
social.bonus: Let the bartender choose for you, with no description first.

social.title: Catch a Touring Band at the State Theatre
social.description: See whoever is coming through the 1929 Congress Street movie palace — the best-sounding room of its size anywhere in Maine.
social.bonus: Get down to the front for the encore.

social.title: Order a Maritime Cocktail at Blyth & Burrows
social.description: Drink in the Old Port's shipwreck-themed cocktail bar on Exchange Street, then find your way into the hidden room upstairs.
social.bonus: Get into the back bar without asking anyone how.

social.title: Get Loud at a Maine Mariners Game
social.description: Take in ECHL hockey at Cross Insurance Arena, where the Bruins' affiliate plays to a crowd that takes it personally.
social.bonus: Stay on your feet for the whole of a penalty kill.

social.title: Play Pinball Until Close at Arcadia National Bar
social.description: Spend a night on fifty-odd pinball machines, skee-ball and consoles at the Congress Street barcade, with pizza and a draught list to match.
social.bonus: Get your initials onto a high-score table before you leave.

social.title: Take a Seat Behind Home Plate at a Sea Dogs Game
social.description: Watch the Red Sox Double-A side with the Fenway-replica wall in left and a Sea Dog Biscuit melting in your hand.
social.bonus: Get the ice cream sandwich between innings, not after the game.

social.title: See a Show on the Lawn at Thompson's Point
social.description: Stand on the grass with the Fore River behind the stage for Portland's big outdoor summer bills, from Wilco to LCD Soundsystem.
social.bonus: Stay for the walk back along the water after the lights come up.

social.title: Drink a Flight in the Allagash Tasting Room
social.description: Go out to Industrial Way for the brewery that made Belgian beer an American habit, and taste the experimental one-offs you can only get on site.
social.bonus: Take the free tour first, then order the beer you just learned about.

social.title: Bowl a String and Take the Bayside Bowl Rooftop
social.description: Bowl downstairs, then climb to the roof deck for tacos out of a 1960s Airstream and the best sunset seat in Bayside.
social.bonus: Win a string and make the loser buy the rooftop round.

social.title: Drink a Bissell Brothers Can on Thompson's Point
social.description: Sit in the loud, bright tasting room out on the point and drink hazy IPA straight from the can, the way they intend it.
social.bonus: Take the can out to the waterfront behind the brewery.

social.title: Catch Oxbow Live in the Blending & Bottling Warehouse
social.description: Drink farmhouse saison among two hundred oak barrels on Washington Avenue while a touring act plays the warehouse floor.
social.bonus: Eat from the Duckfat Frites Shack window in the beer garden on your way out.

social.title: Bounce Between Austin Street and Foundation
social.description: Two of Maine's best breweries share one scruffy industrial yard at 1 Industrial Way — drink hoppy at Foundation, then walk thirty feet to Austin Street.
social.bonus: Do both taprooms and declare a winner out loud.

culture.title: Hear the Kotzschmar Organ at Merrill Auditorium
culture.description: Sit under one of the great municipal pipe organs in the world, installed in 1912, and feel the low notes come up through the floor.
culture.bonus: Sit as close to the front as the ushers will let you.

culture.title: Dig Into the Collections at the Maine Historical Society
culture.description: Go through four hundred years of Maine in the museum and library next to the Longfellow house, from Wabanaki material to shipping logs.
culture.bonus: Ask the librarian to pull one original document for you.

culture.title: See the Painted Sanctuary at the Maine Jewish Museum
culture.description: Climb to the restored 1921 sanctuary on Congress Street for its stained glass, with rotating contemporary Maine art in the galleries below.
culture.bonus: Find the window dedicated to an immigrant family and read the name on it.

culture.title: Tour the Gilded Interiors of Victoria Mansion
culture.description: Walk through an 1860 Italianate villa on Danforth Street with almost all of its original furnishings, frescoes and stained glass still in place.
culture.bonus: Look up in every single room — the painted ceilings are the real show.

culture.title: Catch an Opening at SPACE on Congress Street
culture.description: Go to Portland's contemporary art and performance space for whatever is on — a show, a film, a band, usually all three in a week.
culture.bonus: Talk to one artist about their own work before you leave.

culture.title: Stand in Front of the Winslow Homers at the PMA
culture.description: Work through Maine's best collection — Homer, the Wyeths, Marsden Hartley — in the museum at the top of Congress Square.
culture.bonus: Find the Homer painted at Prouts Neck, then go and see the place itself.

culture.title: Do the First Friday Art Walk Down Congress Street
culture.description: Join the whole city walking between galleries, studios and shopfronts on the first Friday of the month, drink in hand.
culture.bonus: Go into one space you would never otherwise set foot in.

culture.title: Walk Through Longfellow's Childhood Home
culture.description: Tour the 1786 brick house on Congress Street where the poet grew up, still furnished by four generations of the same family.
culture.bonus: Find the room where he wrote as a boy.

foodie.title: Eat Breakfast with the Dock Crews at Becky's Diner
foodie.description: Get to the Commercial Street diner that has been feeding Portland's fishermen since four in the morning, and order the fish hash.
foodie.bonus: Be in a booth before six and see who else is already there.

foodie.title: Queue for a Buttermilk Biscuit at Tandem Coffee + Bakery
foodie.description: Join the line at the old Congress Street filling station for laminated pastry, a fat buttermilk biscuit and house-roasted coffee.
foodie.bonus: Get there before the biscuits sell out — they shut the doors at one.

foodie.title: Order the Brown Butter Lobster Roll at Eventide
foodie.description: Sit at the granite oyster counter for the small steamed bun of lobster in brown butter that reset what a lobster roll could be.
foodie.bonus: Order a half-dozen Maine oysters alongside and take them all from different bays.

foodie.title: Take a Walk-In Seat Downstairs at Central Provisions
foodie.description: Turn up early for the first-come-only downstairs room and build a meal out of crudo, pork belly and a run of small plates.
foodie.bonus: Order five small plates between two of you instead of two big ones.

foodie.title: Eat Beside the Wood-Fired Hearth at Fore Street
foodie.description: Book the room around the brick-and-soapstone hearth where everything comes off a wood oven, grill or turnspit, on a menu rewritten every day.
foodie.bonus: Order whatever came off the turnspit that night, sight unseen.

foodie.title: Take One of Fourteen Stools at the Palace Diner
foodie.description: Drive down to Biddeford for a 1927 dining car with fourteen counter stools and the best breakfast sandwich in the state.
foodie.bonus: Go on a weekday and still expect to wait on the pavement.

foodie.title: Buy a Morning Bun at Standard Baking Co.
foodie.description: Duck into the small bakery under the hotel on Commercial Street for the morning bun and a baguette still warm out of the oven.
foodie.bonus: Eat it on the Eastern Prom instead of in the queue.

foodie.title: Split Duck Fat Fries and Poutine at Duckfat
foodie.description: Queue for a table at the Middle Street storefront and work through a cone of Belgian fries cooked in duck fat with duck gravy poutine.
foodie.bonus: Add a milkshake and finish the whole thing between two of you.

foodie.title: Eat a Maine Potato Doughnut at The Holy Donut
foodie.description: Get a warm doughnut made with real Maine potato — dark chocolate sea salt, fresh lemon — from the Commercial Street waterfront shop.
foodie.bonus: Buy two flavours and eat them both out on the dock.

foodie.title: Build a Lobster Grilled Cheese at Highroller
foodie.description: Go sideways at Highroller Lobster Co. on Exchange Street — lobster grilled cheese, a cheese-crisp lobster taco, lobster tots, their own hot sauce.
foodie.bonus: Order the one thing on the board that reads like a dare.

foodie.title: Slurp the Lobster Noodles at The Honey Paw
foodie.description: Take a kitchen-facing counter stool at Portland's borderless noodle house for lobster noodles and whatever else is on the board.
foodie.bonus: Sit at the counter and order what the cooks recommend over the thing you came in wanting.

foodie.title: Work Through the Raw Bar at Scales
foodie.description: Sit out on Maine Wharf with the water under the floorboards and order whole local fish and oysters from the Fore Street team.
foodie.bonus: Ask what came off the boat that morning and order exactly that.

chill.title: Catch the Sunset Over the Hills from the Western Prom
chill.description: Walk the bluff promenade through the West End's Victorians and watch the sun go down behind the White Mountains.
chill.bonus: Pick which of the mansions behind you you would take.

chill.title: Walk the Old Port Cobblestones Before the Shops Open
chill.description: Get up early and have Exchange and Fore Streets entirely to yourself, with only the delivery vans and the gulls for company.
chill.bonus: Buy a coffee from the very first place that unlocks its door.

chill.title: Walk the Meadows at Gilsland Farm
chill.description: Take the loop trails through Maine Audubon's salt-marsh sanctuary on the Presumpscot estuary, ten minutes out of the city.
chill.bonus: Borrow binoculars at the centre and name three birds before you leave.

chill.title: Watch the Ferries Come In from the Eastern Prom
chill.description: Take a blanket to the long sloping lawn above the bay and watch the island boats cross while the light goes orange.
chill.bonus: Stay until you can tell which boat is going to which island.

chill.title: Read an Afternoon Away in the Library Atrium
chill.description: Take the glass-fronted reading room above Monument Square at the Portland Public Library and give yourself two hours with no phone in them.
chill.bonus: Pull something off the new-arrivals shelf at random and read fifty pages.

chill.title: Sit in the Longfellow Garden Off Congress Street
chill.description: Slip through to the walled garden behind the poet's childhood home — a pocket of complete quiet right off the busiest street in the city.
chill.bonus: Read one Longfellow poem on the bench before you go.

chill.title: Spend a Whole Slow Afternoon on Peaks Island
chill.description: Take the seventeen-minute ferry, walk the shore road, get an ice cream and come back on a late boat having achieved nothing.

chill.title: Shop the Deering Oaks Farmers' Market on a Saturday
chill.description: Walk the long row of Maine growers under the park's trees for cheese, cider doughnuts, oysters and flowers you will not get home intact.
chill.bonus: Buy lunch from three different stalls and eat it on the grass.

chill.title: Linger Over a Pour-Over at Bard Coffee
chill.description: Take a window seat in the Old Port's serious coffee bar and let somebody brew you a single origin by hand.
chill.bonus: Ask the barista to choose the coffee for you.

chill.title: Browse the Shelves at Print: A Bookstore
chill.description: Give an hour to the East End's independent bookshop on Congress Street, where the handwritten staff picks are the whole point.
chill.bonus: Buy the book that a shelf card talked you into.

adventure.title: Haul Lobster Traps Aboard the Lucky Catch
adventure.description: Pull on a rubber apron and work real traps out of Casco Bay on a 90-minute run with a working lobsterman.
adventure.bonus: Buy your catch off the boat for $10 and walk it next door to Portland Lobster Company to be cooked.

adventure.title: Walk the Shore Loop on Mackworth Island
adventure.description: Cross the causeway and circle a mile and a quarter of ledge and spruce with the Portland skyline sitting across the water.
adventure.bonus: Find the fairy village in the woods and leave something behind for it.

adventure.title: Work the Tide Pools Below Two Lights
adventure.description: Pick your way over the tilted rock shelves at Two Lights State Park and go through the pools for crabs, urchins and periwinkles.
adventure.bonus: Time it for low tide and find something alive you can't name.

adventure.title: Swim the Cold Water at Crescent Beach
adventure.description: Take the plunge into properly bracing Maine water off a mile of sand, then dry out on the warm rocks at the far end.
adventure.bonus: Get all the way under on the first attempt — no wading in.

adventure.title: Catch the Beach Break at Higgins Beach
adventure.description: Paddle out at the sandy break that Portland locals have surfed for decades, twenty minutes south of the city.
adventure.bonus: Stay in the water until you ride one all the way to the sand.

adventure.title: Kayak Out to Fort Gorges in the Middle of the Harbor
adventure.description: Paddle across Portland Harbor with Portland Paddle and climb through an abandoned granite Civil War fort on its own island.
adventure.bonus: Get to the upper tier and shout once inside the empty parade ground to hear the echo come back.

adventure.title: Ski the Night Lights at Pleasant Mountain
adventure.description: Drive an hour inland for the best night skiing in Maine, lit top to bottom on the state's oldest ski mountain.
adventure.bonus: Take one run through the Sherwood Forest glades before the lights go out.

adventure.title: Run the Eastern Promenade Trail at Sunrise
adventure.description: Take the flat waterfront path along the bay before the city wakes, with the islands coming out of the dark on your right.
adventure.bonus: Make it all the way to Ocean Gateway and back without stopping.

adventure.title: Walk the Cliff Path to Portland Head Light
adventure.description: Follow the shore trail through Fort Williams Park to the most photographed lighthouse in America, standing over the surf since 1791.
adventure.bonus: Carry on to the Goddard Mansion ruins before you head back.

adventure.title: Find the Ruins of Battery Steele on Peaks Island
adventure.description: Walk into the woods on Peaks and come out at a vast WWII gun battery, now a graffiti-covered concrete tunnel driven through the hill.
adventure.bonus: Walk the full length of the dark tunnel without a torch.

adventure.title: Climb the Portland Observatory on Munjoy Hill
adventure.description: Haul yourself up seven flights of an 1807 signal tower — the last maritime one left in America — for the whole of Casco Bay through the windows.
adventure.bonus: Count the steps on the way up and see if your number matches the guide's.

adventure.title: Sail Casco Bay on the Schooner Bagheera
adventure.description: Take a two-hour sail on a 1924 Maine-built wooden schooner and help haul the mainsail if the crew lets you near it.
adventure.bonus: Ask the captain which island has the best story, then make them prove it.

adventure.title: Ride the Mailboat Run Through the Whole Bay
adventure.description: Take the Casco Bay Lines mailboat on its full island circuit and watch the post, the freight and the locals come and go at every dock.
adventure.bonus: Stay out on deck for the entire loop, whatever the wind is doing.

adventure.title: Book an L.L.Bean Outdoor Discovery Course in Freeport
adventure.description: Sign up for a half-day clinic — fly casting, clay shooting, paddling, winter navigation — run by guides out of the flagship store.
adventure.bonus: Pick the discipline you have never once tried.

adventure.title: Ride a Rental Bike Around the Peaks Island Loop
adventure.description: Take the ferry over, grab a bike from Brad's on Island Avenue and ride the back-shore loop with the open Atlantic at your shoulder.
adventure.bonus: Stop on the back shore and skip a stone into the open ocean.

adventure.title: Scramble to the Bald Summit of Bradbury Mountain
adventure.description: Climb the short, steep Summit Trail to an open granite top with a view that runs all the way back to Casco Bay.
adventure.bonus: Go up the Summit Trail and come down the Tote Road for the long way home.
